newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag declines comment on Bewag.
newsitem.headline: Viag declines comment on Bewag.

text.p: German utility Viag AG on Wednesday declined comment on a newspaper report that it planned to link up with Veba AG in a joint bid for a higher stake in Berliner Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag).
"We do not want to comment on this for the time being," a spokeswoman told Reuters.

The Boersen-Zeitung newspaper had cited Veba manager and Bewag supervisory board member Alfred Dworak as saying that Viag and Veba were interested in taking on a package of more than 25.8 percent in Bewag from the state of Berlin.
Dworak told the newspaper that a joint offer would be made on Friday, with Veba aiming to take on a 14.8 percent stake and Viag 11 percent.
The companies each already own 10 percent of Bewag's capital via subsidiaries and control 14 percent of its voting rights.
Viag chief executive Georg Obermeier has several times described Bewag as an "interesting" investment and business area. Bewag supplies electricity for the Berlin region.

Separately, the Financial Times reported that British electricity generator PowerGen Plc was considering making an offer for Bewag, which is still majority-owned by Berlin but due for privatisation next year. PowerGen's shares dropped on the report.
